- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

3	/// The full result of a short status command: stdout, stderr, exit code, and whether the
4	/// timeout fired. Unlike `CommandRunning` (which collapses everything to `String?`), this
5	/// keeps the exit code and timeout flag so `WorkroomStatusResolver` can tell "not a repo"
6	/// (git exit 128) from "gh not installed" (exit 127) from "timed out" from "clean" — the
7	/// distinctions the status UI's unknown/stale/absent matrix depends on.
8	struct CommandResult: Sendable, Equatable {
9	  let stdout: String
10	  let stderr: String
11	  let exitCode: Int32
12	  let timedOut: Bool
13	
14	  /// `/usr/bin/env` exits 127 when the command (git/jj/gh) isn't on PATH.
15	  static let commandNotFound: Int32 = 127
16	  /// git exits 128 for "not a git repository" and similar fatal usage errors.
17	  static let gitFatal: Int32 = 128
18	
19	  var ok: Bool { exitCode == 0 && !timedOut }
20	}
21	
22	/// A seam (mirrors `CommandRunning`) so `WorkroomStatusResolver` is unit-testable without
23	/// spawning real git/jj/gh — but typed (`CommandResult`, not `String?`).
24	protocol StatusCommandRunning: Sendable {
25	  func run(_ executable: String, _ args: [String], in directory: String, timeout: TimeInterval)
26	    async -> CommandResult
27	
28	  /// Like `run`, but for a command that will touch the **network** and therefore may want to
29	  /// authenticate — `git fetch/push/pull`, `jj git fetch/push`.
30	  ///
31	  /// A read like `git status` can never prompt, so it wants the minimal, predictable environment
32	  /// `run` gives it. A push can: it may need an SSH agent the GUI environment can't see, and it may
33	  /// try to ask for a passphrase or a host-key confirmation with nowhere to ask. See
34	  /// `StatusCommandRunner.networkEnvironment` for what changes and why.
35	  func runNetwork(
36	    _ executable: String, _ args: [String], in directory: String,
37	    timeout: TimeInterval
38	  ) async -> CommandResult
39	}
40	
41	extension StatusCommandRunning {
42	  /// Test doubles never reach a real network, so the distinction is meaningless for them — forward
43	  /// and let them stay two-line stubs. Only `StatusCommandRunner` overrides this.
44	  func runNetwork(
45	    _ executable: String, _ args: [String], in directory: String,
46	    timeout: TimeInterval
47	  ) async -> CommandResult {
48	    await run(executable, args, in: directory, timeout: timeout)
49	  }
50	}
51	
52	/// Default `StatusCommandRunning`: spawns via `/usr/bin/env` (augmented PATH finds Homebrew
53	/// git/jj/gh), git locks/prompt disabled, and enforces `timeout` by terminating the process.
54	///
55	/// Unlike `ProcessCommandRunner` (which reads stdout *in* the termination handler — safe only
56	/// because a branch name is tiny), this drains stdout AND stderr **concurrently on background
57	/// queues while the process runs** (the `WorkroomCLI` pattern). Status output can be large (a
58	/// repo with thousands of changed files, a big `gh` JSON payload); reading post-termination
59	/// would let the OS pipe buffer fill, block the child on write, and deadlock until the timeout.
60	/// Retained output is capped (`maxBytes`) so a pathological repo can't blow memory — the reader
61	/// keeps draining past the cap (so the child never blocks) but discards the overflow.
62	struct StatusCommandRunner: StatusCommandRunning, Sendable {
63	  var maxBytes: Int = 4 * 1024 * 1024
64	
65	  /// Auth-relevant variables forwarded from the user's shell for network commands only.
66	  ///
67	  /// A Finder- or Dock-launched `.app` inherits launchd's environment, not the user's shell, and this
68	  /// runner otherwise overrides only PATH. That was harmless while it ran `git status` and `gh` (which
69	  /// carries its own token), but it breaks authentication outright: `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` is how a process
70	  /// finds an SSH agent, and for anyone using 1Password's agent, gpg-agent, or a custom socket it is
71	  /// set in `.zshrc` and nowhere else. Without it their `git push` cannot reach the agent, and the
72	  /// error would tell them to configure a credential helper they already have.
73	  ///
74	  /// Deliberately an allowlist, not the whole probed environment (which `ShellEnvironment.environment()`
75	  /// hands to setup/teardown scripts): network ops now run automatically on inspector focus, and a
76	  /// wholesale transplant would put every variable in the user's shell — secrets included — into a
77	  /// child on an automatic path.
78	  static let forwardedAuthKeys = [
79	    "SSH_AUTH_SOCK", "SSH_AGENT_PID", "GIT_SSH_COMMAND", "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL", "XDG_CONFIG_HOME",
80	  ]
81	
82	  /// Variables removed for network commands so `ssh` cannot find a graphical prompt helper.
83	  static let networkClearedKeys = ["SSH_ASKPASS", "DISPLAY"]
84	
85	  /// The environment for a network command: `base` plus forwarded auth vars, with ssh pinned to
86	  /// fail fast instead of asking a human.
87	  ///
88	  /// `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` (set by `run`) governs **git's own** credential prompts and says nothing
89	  /// to `ssh`. So an SSH remote with a passphrase-protected key and no agent, or a host whose key
90	  /// isn't in `known_hosts`, would otherwise stall until the timeout — 120s for fetch/push, 300s for
91	  /// pull. `BatchMode=yes` turns both into an immediate, classifiable failure, and
92	  /// `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never` stops ssh reaching for a GUI helper (OpenSSH 8.4+; macOS ships 10.x).
93	  ///
94	  /// A user's own `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` is preserved and appended to rather than replaced — it commonly
95	  /// carries `-i <key>` or a proxy command that must survive.
96	  ///
97	  /// Pure and static so the whole policy is unit-testable without spawning anything.
98	  static func networkEnvironment(base: [String: String], probed: [String: String])
99	    -> [String: String]
100	  {
101	    var env = base
102	    for key in forwardedAuthKeys {
103	      // The inherited environment wins: if it's already set, the app was launched from a shell that
104	      // had it, and that value is at least as current as the probe's.
105	      if env[key] == nil, let value = probed[key], !value.isEmpty { env[key] = value }
106	    }
107	    for key in networkClearedKeys { env.removeValue(forKey: key) }
108	    let ssh = env["GIT_SSH_COMMAND"]?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
109	    env["GIT_SSH_COMMAND"] = (ssh?.isEmpty == false ? ssh! : "ssh") + " -o BatchMode=yes"
110	    env["SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE"] = "never"
111	    return env
112	  }
113	
114	  func run(_ executable: String, _ args: [String], in directory: String, timeout: TimeInterval)
115	    async -> CommandResult
116	  {
117	    await run(executable, args, in: directory, timeout: timeout, network: false)
118	  }
119	
120	  func runNetwork(
121	    _ executable: String, _ args: [String], in directory: String,
122	    timeout: TimeInterval
123	  ) async -> CommandResult {
124	    await run(executable, args, in: directory, timeout: timeout, network: true)
125	  }

127	  private func run(
128	    _ executable: String, _ args: [String], in directory: String,
129	    timeout: TimeInterval, network: Bool
130	  ) async -> CommandResult {
131	    let proc = Process()
132	    proc.executableURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: "/usr/bin/env")
133	    proc.arguments = [executable] + args
134	    proc.currentDirectoryURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: directory)
135	
136	    var env = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment
137	    env["PATH"] = ShellEnvironment.path()
138	    env["GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS"] = "0"
139	    env["GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT"] = "0"
140	    // A workroom can be a clone of an *untrusted* repo, and the status sweep runs git automatically
141	    // on load/focus/selection. `git diff` would otherwise run an inherited external-diff program;
142	    // unset it so only the explicit `--no-ext-diff` flag (see WorkroomStatusResolver) governs diffs.
143	    env.removeValue(forKey: "GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF")
144	    if network { env = Self.networkEnvironment(base: env, probed: ShellEnvironment.environment()) }
145	    proc.environment = env
146	
147	    let outPipe = Pipe()
148	    let errPipe = Pipe()
149	    proc.standardOutput = outPipe
150	    proc.standardError = errPipe
151	    // Never let a child read the app's stdin. Unset, it INHERITS ours — which under `make app-run`
152	    // (or `Scripts/run.sh`) is a real terminal, so a prompting `ssh` or `git` could sit waiting on a
153	    // tty that the same binary won't have when launched from Finder. Pinning it makes the two launch
154	    // contexts behave identically and turns any prompt into an immediate EOF. `ShellEnvironment.probe`
155	    // already does this for the same reason.
156	    proc.standardInput = FileHandle.nullDevice

158	    // `proc` is shared with the @Sendable cancellation handler; box it so the non-Sendable Process
159	    // can cross that boundary (mirrors the @unchecked Sendable helpers below).
160	    let box = ProcessBox(proc)
161	
162	    return await withTaskCancellationHandler {
163	      await withCheckedContinuation { (continuation: CheckedContinuation<CommandResult, Never>) in
164	        let state = StatusRunState()
165	        let drain = DispatchGroup()
166	        let cap = maxBytes
167	        let gate = CommandResumeGate(continuation)
168	
169	        // Concurrent drains (the deadlock fix). availableData blocks until data or EOF;
170	        // started before run() so we never miss a fast child's output, harmless until it runs.
171	        drain.enter()
172	        DispatchQueue.global().async {
173	          state.setStdout(Self.readCapped(outPipe.fileHandleForReading, cap: cap))
174	          drain.leave()
175	        }
176	        drain.enter()
177	        DispatchQueue.global().async {
178	          state.setStderr(Self.readCapped(errPipe.fileHandleForReading, cap: cap))
179	          drain.leave()
180	        }
181	
182	        let timeoutItem = DispatchWorkItem {
183	          state.markTimedOut()
184	          if proc.isRunning { proc.terminate() }  // SIGTERM
185	        }
186	        DispatchQueue.global().asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + timeout, execute: timeoutItem)
187	
188	        // Hard-kill fallback: a wedged child (e.g. `gh` blocked on a dead socket) can ignore SIGTERM,
189	        // so `terminationHandler` — the only place the continuation resumes — would never fire and the
190	        // awaiting Task would hang forever, defeating the timeout. SIGKILL is uncatchable, guaranteeing
191	        // the process exits and we resume. A 2s grace after SIGTERM lets well-behaved children exit.
192	        let killItem = DispatchWorkItem {
193	          if proc.isRunning { ProcessTree.killTree(proc.processIdentifier) }
194	        }
195	        DispatchQueue.global().asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + timeout + 2, execute: killItem)
196	
197	        proc.terminationHandler = { finished in
198	          timeoutItem.cancel()
199	          killItem.cancel()
200	          // The process has exited, so its own pipe write ends are closed and EOF is imminent. But a
201	          // grandchild that inherited the pipe (a helper spawned by gh/git) can hold the write end
202	          // open after the parent dies — an unbounded `drain.wait()` would then never return and the
203	          // continuation would never resume, wedging this probe slot forever. Bound the wait and
204	          // resume with whatever drained; a still-blocked reader writes to `state` we no longer read
205	          // (safe — lock-guarded) and exits when the grandchild finally closes the pipe.
206	          _ = drain.wait(timeout: .now() + 2)
207	          gate.resume(
208	            CommandResult(
209	              stdout: String(decoding: state.stdout, as: UTF8.self),
210	              stderr: String(decoding: state.stderr, as: UTF8.self),
211	              exitCode: finished.terminationStatus,
212	              timedOut: state.timedOut))
213	        }
214	
215	        do {
216	          try proc.run()
217	        } catch {
218	          // Launch failed (e.g. cwd vanished). Close the write ends so the drain readers hit
219	          // EOF instead of blocking forever, then resolve as command-not-found.
220	          timeoutItem.cancel()
221	          killItem.cancel()
222	          try? outPipe.fileHandleForWriting.close()
223	          try? errPipe.fileHandleForWriting.close()
224	          gate.resume(
225	            CommandResult(
226	              stdout: "", stderr: "\(error)", exitCode: CommandResult.commandNotFound,
227	              timedOut: false))
228	        }
229	      }
230	    } onCancel: {
231	      // The awaiting Task was cancelled (e.g. a superseded sweep, or rapid selection cycling). Kill
232	      // the in-flight child so a cancelled probe doesn't leave a git/jj/gh process running to its own
233	      // timeout. terminationHandler then resumes the continuation with the abandoned result, which
234	      // the cancelled caller discards. SIGKILL (not SIGTERM) so a wedged child dies promptly.
235	      box.terminate()
236	    }
237	  }

239	  /// Drain a pipe to EOF, retaining at most `cap` bytes but reading the rest so the child
240	  /// never blocks on a full pipe buffer.
241	  private static func readCapped(_ handle: FileHandle, cap: Int) -> Data {
242	    var collected = Data()
243	    while true {
244	      // `read(upToCount:)` (throwing) instead of `availableData`: the latter raises an
245	      // *Objective-C* `NSFileHandleOperationException` on a read error (common right after the
246	      // child is `terminate()`d out from under the open read end), which Swift can't catch — it
247	      // crashes the app. Treat a read error as EOF and return what we have.
248	      let chunk: Data
249	      do { chunk = try handle.read(upToCount: 1 << 16) ?? Data() } catch { break }
250	      if chunk.isEmpty { break }  // EOF: pipe closed
251	      if collected.count < cap {
252	        collected.append(chunk.prefix(cap - collected.count))
253	      }
254	    }
255	    return collected
256	  }
257	}

259	/// Boxes a non-Sendable `Process` so it can be captured by the @Sendable task-cancellation handler.
260	private final class ProcessBox: @unchecked Sendable {
261	  private let process: Process
262	  init(_ process: Process) { self.process = process }
263	  /// SIGKILL the child (and any descendants it spawned) if still running — the cancellation path
264	  /// abandons the result, so kill promptly rather than wait out a SIGTERM grace.
265	  ///
266	  /// Hopped to a global queue because `withTaskCancellationHandler`'s `onCancel` runs **synchronously
267	  /// on whichever thread called `cancel()`**, and the hottest canceller is the main thread:
268	  /// `selectedTargetID.didSet` → `scheduleSelectedStatusRefresh` → `selectionStatusTask?.cancel()`
269	  /// supersedes the in-flight probe on *every* selection change. `ProcessTree.killTree` walks the tree
270	  /// by spawning a `pgrep -P` per node and blocking on `waitUntilExit` for each, so inline it stalled
271	  /// the main thread for the length of that walk while switching workroom tabs — and a blocking wait
272	  /// spins a nested run loop, which drains queued main-queue blocks at a point SwiftUI hasn't committed
273	  /// its update yet (that reordering is what surfaced the split-member selection snap-back). Deferring
274	  /// the kill costs nothing: the continuation resumes from `terminationHandler`, never from here, and
275	  /// the cancelled caller discards the result. Matches `killItem`, which already kills off a global
276	  /// queue.
277	  func terminate() {
278	    let process = self.process
279	    DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated).async {
280	      if process.isRunning { ProcessTree.killTree(process.processIdentifier) }
281	    }
282	  }
283	}
284	
285	/// Mutable scratch shared between the drain queues and the termination handler. Locked
286	/// because the two reads and the handler touch it from different threads.
287	private final class StatusRunState: @unchecked Sendable {
288	  private let lock = NSLock()
289	  private var _stdout = Data()
290	  private var _stderr = Data()
291	  private var _timedOut = false
292	
293	  func setStdout(_ d: Data) {
294	    lock.lock()
295	    _stdout = d
296	    lock.unlock()
297	  }
298	  func setStderr(_ d: Data) {
299	    lock.lock()
300	    _stderr = d
301	    lock.unlock()
302	  }
303	  func markTimedOut() {
304	    lock.lock()
305	    _timedOut = true
306	    lock.unlock()
307	  }
308	
309	  var stdout: Data {
310	    lock.lock()
311	    defer { lock.unlock() }
312	    return _stdout
313	  }
314	  var stderr: Data {
315	    lock.lock()
316	    defer { lock.unlock() }
317	    return _stderr
318	  }
319	  var timedOut: Bool {
320	    lock.lock()
321	    defer { lock.unlock() }
322	    return _timedOut
323	  }
324	}
325	
326	/// Resumes a `CommandResult` continuation exactly once (termination vs launch-failure race).
327	private final class CommandResumeGate: @unchecked Sendable {
328	  private let lock = NSLock()
329	  private var done = false
330	  private let continuation: CheckedContinuation<CommandResult, Never>
331	
332	  init(_ continuation: CheckedContinuation<CommandResult, Never>) {
333	    self.continuation = continuation
334	  }
335	
336	  func resume(_ value: CommandResult) {
337	    lock.lock()
338	    let first = !done
339	    done = true
340	    lock.unlock()
341	    if first { continuation.resume(returning: value) }
342	  }
343	}

Based on my review, I traced the key attack surfaces this diff introduces:

**Network command execution (`StatusCommandRunner.runNetwork`)** — pinned stdin to `/dev/null`, forwards env via explicit allowlist (`SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `SSH_AGENT_PID`), sets `BatchMode=yes` and `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never`. All args passed via `proc.arguments` array — no shell.

**CLI arg construction (`CLIVCSWriter`)** — every `remote`/`branch`/`revision` value passed to git/jj comes from git/jj's own output (parseGitRemoteRefs / parseJJBookmarks / currentRef), and git enforces ref-name rules that reject leading-dash names, so arg-injection into positional args isn't reachable. `anonymousRevision` is limited to literal `"@"`/`
